description: Replace torch.geqrf with a CUTE DSL batched Householder QR path specialized for n=512 high-batch cases, using one CTA group per matrix panel and preserving FP32 compact H/tau outputs.

Prototype a CUTE DSL blocked QR for n=1024 and larger low-batch cases with tiled reflector application, prioritizing robust FP32 correctness over full genericity while falling back safely where unsupported.
Use CUTE DSL for targeted fast-path detection and handling of upper-triangular or near-rank-deficient structures, minimizing unnecessary geqrf work while returning valid compact factors.

Combine the best 512 rank-deficient CUTE DSL tail-zero shortcut with the conservative upper-triangular zero-tau fast path, resolving overlaps into one safe submission and preserving all benchmark-shape correctness.
Build on the best mixed zero-tail branch with a true CUTE DSL blocked reflector update for 512x512 rank-deficient panels, replacing partial torch.geqrf work while keeping dense fallback correctness.
Optimize the best n=512 shortcut branch by replacing expensive torch tail detectors with cheaper CUTE DSL probes or fused reductions, preserving rankdef and clustered routing correctness.
From the current best shortcut branch, attack 1024 and 2048 rank-deficient or nearrank cases with a CUTE DSL rectangular compact-H embedding that reduces geqrf size without shape mismatches.
Combine the best sparse CUTE 512 clustered detector with worker 1's 1024-plus rectangular shortcut experiments, keeping only improvements that preserve the 109272-us baseline branch correctness.
Stack the best sparse 512 detector with the successful 1024/2048 zero-tail compact-H embedding, resolving conflicts to beat 109272 us without reintroducing nearrank truncation failures.
Explore a structurally different CUTE DSL fast path for large 2048/4096 triangular or zero-tail matrices, generating compact identity or reduced factors without adding overhead to dense fallbacks.
Tune the current best CUTE DSL structural-probe branch by reducing sentinel and detector overhead for 2048/4096 validation-only paths while preserving dense benchmark fallback speed.
Explore batch-aware CUTE DSL routing on the current best branch: specialize benchmark batch sizes to avoid unnecessary probes and try separate fast paths for homogeneous versus mixed 512 batches.
Attempt a true dense n=512 CUTE DSL geqr2-style panel QR replacement for high-batch benchmark cases, initially targeting one panel or partial factor while preserving fallback correctness.
Combine the best batch-aware 512 routing branch with the 16-chunk large-detector tuning, keeping only changes that improve over 108896 us and preserve all CUTE DSL fast-path correctness.
Explore CUTE DSL or torch-light fast paths for small n=32/176/352 benchmark shapes on the current best branch, targeting reduced launch and geqrf overhead without harming large-shape routing.
Tune the new best combined branch by adding only low-risk early returns or detector ordering changes for n<512 and dense fallbacks, targeting sub-108846 us without changing factor math.
Combine the current best branch with the gated dense n=512 CUTE first-Householder prefix, accepting it only if it beats 108846 us while preserving all rankdef and clustered routing.
Attempt a real CUTE DSL compact-H QR implementation for the small n=32 benchmark shape first, returning exact FP32 Householder factors and falling back for n=176/352 if needed.
Replace the rejected one-reflector dense prepass with a multi-reflector CUTE DSL n=512 panel experiment, keeping it gated and logging failures if compact-H correctness or overhead regresses.
Explore a CUTE DSL specialized path for n=176 or n=352 dense benchmark matrices using a compact unrolled Householder or Gram-Schmidt variant that still returns valid geqrf-style H/tau.
Preserve the new best QR32 one-warp CUTE kernel while rechecking integration with current-best routing and detector tuning, accepting only variants that beat 101493 us across the full benchmark set.
Micro-tune the winning one-warp n=32 CUTE QR kernel for memory traffic and register staging, keeping compact-H math identical and accepting only full-benchmark wins over 101366 us.
Continue from the true best QR32 branch and try safe launch-parameter or threshold micro-tunes around the one-warp CUTE n=32 kernel, reverting any runtime errors or benchmark regressions.
Attempt to generalize the working QR32 one-warp CUTE compact-H kernel to n=176 with tiled panels or multiple warps, keeping fallback for failures and prioritizing correctness first.
